topics.title: Similarities and Enlargement
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: State and use the properties of similar figures. (k, u)
State the properties of enlargement to construct objects and images. (k)
Understand and use the relationship between linear, area and volume scale factors. (u, s)

body.text: Two figures are similar if one is an enlargement of the other: matching angles are equal, and matching sides are all in the same ratio (the scale factor). Enlargement is a transformation that makes a shape bigger or smaller from a fixed centre of enlargement, without changing its shape.

Sara is 150 cm tall and casts a shadow 50 cm long. At the same time, a tree casts a shadow 210 cm long. Since Sara and the tree are both vertical and the sun's rays hit them at the same angle, Sara and her shadow form a triangle similar to the tree and its shadow. The scale factor is 210 ÷ 50 = 4.2, so the tree's height is 150 x 4.2 = 630 cm.

body.expr: scale factor = 210 ÷ 50 = 4.2;   tree height = 150 x 4.2 = 630 cm

body.text: If the linear scale factor between two similar shapes is k, the area scale factor is k^2 and the volume scale factor is k^3 — because area involves two lengths multiplied together, and volume involves three. A model boat built at 1:20 scale (k = 1/20) needs 20^2 = 400 times less paint by area, and holds 20^3 = 8000 times less water by volume than the real boat.

body.expr: linear scale factor k  ->  area scale factor k^2,  volume scale factor k^3
